title: Treat Boundary Violations as First-Class Decision Records
decision: Classify detected SCP boundary violations and red-flag patterns as recordable decision events within DMP.
context: Boundary violations often emerge through drift rather than explicit intent. When violations are observed but not recorded, organizations lose the opportunity to learn and deny responsibility through omission.
rationale: If crossing a boundary changes the ethical or causal state of a system, that crossing is itself a decision worth remembering.
consequences: Systems gain durable memory of ethical drift events without requiring enforcement or retroactive justification.
scp_risk_notes: Boundary violations signal a transition into heightened responsibility and must not remain implicit.
alternatives: Treat boundary violations as operational incidents only
Handle violations informally without durable records
